analysis:
Only .github/workflows/release-swift.yml changed. It adds scripts/provider_release_identity.py, whose output is appended to $GITHUB_ENV, and parameterizes the app name, CLI name and enclave name for dev and prod. The global CLI_NAME and ENCLAVE_NAME env were removed. Flat bin/ names stay the SwiftPM product names (PRODUCT_CLI_NAME and PRODUCT_ENCLAVE_NAME). Hashes registered with the coordinator are taken from the flat bin/ copy. The pipeline gains cmp checks between the flat and in-app binaries, tar listing checks for the in-app executables, and a build-environment smoke check that now requires `cli=${CLI_NAME}`. CodeDirectory hash extraction and the stapler, spctl and codesign verification are unchanged. The bundle ID, signing identity, provisioning profile and keychain group remain identical for dev and prod. This is the basis of the finding about shared SE and App Attest credentials (T-055, T-058, T-034, TB-011).

Items for the next pass:
- The script was not supplied. It writes to GITHUB_ENV, and VERSION can come from the workflow_dispatch version_override input. Confirm the script validates VERSION and emits no newlines or injectable values.
- PRODUCT_CLI_NAME is used in the build-provider 'Bind unsigned bundle' step (patch hunk @@ -230). The resolve step was added only to build-and-release (around line 354) and the later validation job (around line 1213). Unless the composite action exports it, `set -u` makes that step fail. This fails closed, so it is an availability concern only.
- CLI_NAME is no longer a global env, so any remaining job that references it (such as publication) must receive it from a resolve step.
- Check that the coordinator's release registration and the installer use the flat product names consistently. Unchanged callers were not reviewed.

findings.detail: The header comment states that dev releases install beside production while the bundle identifier and signing identity stay identical. The Info.plist step keeps CFBundleIdentifier=io.darkbloom.provider, and the same provisioning profile and keychain-access-group are embedded. Dev apps are published on every master push without a tag. On one Mac, a dev build can therefore load the production persistent SE key (label io.darkbloom.provider.attestation-signing.v2) and the same-app-ID App Attest credential. This lets a dev-channel binary sign attestation or challenges for the production identity. The same SE public key is also visible to both the dev and prod coordinators, which links the two environments' sessions. Existing controls such as binary-hash and CodeDirectory qualification and the per-connection process X25519 key limit the damage. Even so, this weakens the dev/prod credential separation that T-055 and T-058 assume. Fix: give the dev app a distinct bundle ID, keychain label or access group (and profile), or document and test that dev builds cannot use production credentials. Update the threat model either way.
findings.title: Dev and prod apps share one bundle ID, signing identity and keychain group, so side-by-side installs share hardware-bound credentials
